correctness.rationale: Kummer borrows imply strictly monotone counts under coordinatewise increase of n digits. This reduces all second-extremal rows to N+p^j or 2N; the digit transfer matrix yields the stated exact borrow polynomials, and exhaustive coefficient-truncation comparison gives all p,alpha,h regimes and ties. Tested independently against 84 full intervals (138920 rows) and 3680 exact-binomial counts; these are corroboration rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The classical Rowland, Everett, and Spiegelhofer–Wallner pointwise counting formulas are explicitly acknowledged as stronger background data, but inspected full articles do not state or prove the sharp second-order block-wide optimization with every equality case. Actual published-finding corpus semantic comparisons and alias searches found related binomial divisibility and p-adic statements on distinct objects, not dominating implications. Coverage in uninspected literature remains possible.
residual_risks: A structural corollary hidden in a different extremal or digital-combinatorics paper may duplicate this second minimum.
Pointwise formulas in Rowland imply computability of all values; intellectual distinction from their unstated optimization requires independent contextual scrutiny.

value.rationale: A natural second-order extremum of prime-power Pascal-row support has a uniform piecewise law and complete equality classification, revealing a phase transition at h=alpha and exceptional binary ties. This goes beyond isolated rows, mechanical restatement of the pointwise digit formula, and finite table entries; it is relevant to stability of sparse Pascal rows.
